provider: Pinned Synapse 1.164.1, isolated SQLite container with loopback-only client port, owned network, fictional identities, federation/public registration disabled. Application RLS/queue/persistence use actual PostgreSQL 18.6.
verifiedBehaviors: An enabled API context registers a pending device without waiting for an unreachable provider.

An enabled worker context claims through the actual queue, executes persistent Spring Batch, obtains a real bounded Matrix credential, stores it encrypted and activates exactly one deterministic device.
The stored credential passes actual Synapse whoami with the expected scoped user/device; completed-lease replay cannot rotate it.
Pausing the actual provider produces bounded failure/backoff; resumption and a fixture-only queue-deadline advance succeed with the same device and second queue attempt.
Revoked origins fail and requested cancellation cancels the owned job without credential publication. Cancellation preserves the interrupt signal; the fixture explicitly acknowledges it.
Disabled provider creates no Matrix HTTP client/configuration/task. Enabled provider requires the identity keyring and bounded signing file.
The client owner terminates on disposal, including repeated disposal; malformed/missing/oversized/non-ASCII/multiline signing files fail without exposing content.

correctedFailures.result: 3 settings passes; 7 ordinary worker cases pass; 3 new worker cases cannot load context because the handwritten fictional Base64 key was malformed. Fixed by generating the 32-byte fixture key encoding.

4 settings and 1 enabled API case pass. Actual provider activation and outage cases pass; cancellation case fails its subsequent SQL assertion because the runtime correctly preserves interruption. Fixture now asserts and consumes that expected signal before the next assertion.

limitations: These tests prove provisioning, queue ownership and bounded internal credentials, not product E2EE/chat or protected SDK gateway behavior.
The outage case advances only its fictional queue available_at to avoid a wall-clock backoff wait; production eight-attempt backoff remains unchanged.
The existing opt-in elapsed export-retention case remains skipped in the full worker suite; this change introduces no skipped test.
Operator-owned secret mounting, provider infrastructure, HRIS gateway, explicit manual retry, SDK/chat and later phases remain outstanding; both service switches remain false by default.
